Most likely this is because VRChat has unintentionally moved them to a different sorting layer other than the "Player" layer, which is the collision layer in Unity that refers to both the Local and Remote user in-game.
This sorting layer is largely important (as a world creator myself) because Mirrors need the "Player" layer in order to render the players in the world in the first place. Most mirrors in worlds show ALL layers, while some many others use the "Default", "Player", “Environment”, and "MirrorReflection" layers ONLY, which in a nutshell, are the only 4 layers needed for a High Quality Mirror.
So if the calibration dots are in for say "UiMenu" layer instead, they will NEVER show in such mirrors because that layer was purposely culled by the world's creator.
Source: current version of the World SDK 3.0
